blocks.text: Obfy renames and hardens your compiled .NET assemblies before you ship them, so the shipped build is harder for others to reverse-engineer. Your original files are never changed. Protected copies go to a separate output folder.
Start on Files. Drop assemblies, a solution or a project onto the window, or choose **Add files**. Standard protection is selected for you and is a good first run.

Press **Obfuscate** or {Ctrl+Enter}. When the run finishes, Results opens with a summary, the symbol map and a preview of the output. Always run your own tests against the protected build before you ship it.

blocks.title: Obfuscation is not secrecy
blocks.text: String, constant, resource, method and packing encryption hides values from casual inspection. The keys live in the output assembly (or the native packing overlay) and are recoverable by anyone who runs or inspects it.

Obfy accepts `.dll`, `.exe`, `.cs`, `.sln`, `.slnx`, `.csproj`, `.vbproj` and `.fsproj`. A solution or project expands into the assemblies it builds. Test projects are listed but skipped, and you can include them again with the checkbox. A `.json` file loads a saved configuration.

Add files ({Ctrl+O}) opens a picker for assemblies, C# source, solutions and projects. You can also drop them anywhere on the window. The checkbox on a row drops a file from the run without removing it, and {Delete} removes the selected files.

When two or more assemblies are included, they are processed together as a closed set, so references between them keep working after renaming. Turn on **Merge assemblies** in Protection to combine them into one file instead.
Where the output goes

Leave the output folder empty and Obfy chooses for you. One file is written next to the input as `MyApp.obfuscated.dll`. A closed set is written to an `obfy-out` folder next to the first input. A merge is written next to the first input as `*.obfuscated.*`.
**Write a symbol map** saves a file that maps the new short names back to the originals. Keep it private. You need it to read stack traces from the protected build.

A level is a ready-made set of protections. **Minimal** renames symbols only and is the safest. **Standard** adds encoded strings and attribute clean-up. **Aggressive** turns on most protections and needs careful testing. Each card shows three small meters for protection, run-time cost and compatibility risk, so you can compare them at a glance.

Change any single option and you move to **Custom**. A **Changed** badge marks every option that differs from the level you started from. Choose a level card again to reset, or choose Custom to return to your own mix.
Target runtime

Some protections do not work on every runtime. Pick the runtime your app runs on (Default, NativeAOT, Unity IL2CPP or Blazor WebAssembly) and Obfy switches those off for you. Their settings are kept, so switching back restores them.
Configuration files

Save ({Ctrl+S}) writes your settings to `obfy.json`. Open ({Ctrl+L}) loads one, and so does dropping a `.json` file onto the window. Check the file in next to your solution so builds on other machines use the same settings.
Select any row in Protection to read what it does, what it costs and what each option means. The main groups are:

items: **Names.** Symbol renaming replaces type, member and namespace names.
**Data.** String, constant and resource encoding hide the values your code uses.
**Code.** Control flow, reference proxies, method body encoding and virtualization change how code is stored and run.
**Runtime checks.** Debugger, integrity and memory checks, and decoy types for decompilers.
**Packaging.** Merge, embed dependencies, native packing and strong-name signing.

blocks.title: Obfuscation is not encryption
blocks.text: Encoding hides data from casual inspection. The key ships inside the assembly, so a determined person can recover the text. Never embed real secrets such as keys or passwords.
These work anywhere in the window.

items.label: Copy selected log lines or symbols

blocks.text: After a run, Results shows four tabs. **Summary** counts what was renamed, encoded and removed and lists each output file. **Symbols** is the symbol map as a tree: original names first, then the new short names, with members nested under their type.

**Preview** decompiles an output assembly so you can see what a reader would see. It only decompiles when you choose a file. **Log** keeps earlier runs and separates them with a line, and can show only warnings and errors.
To read a stack trace from the protected build, search the Symbols tab for the short name, or open the exported symbol map. Warnings in the log usually point at code that looks names up as text.
